Protesters Blockade Major Slovak Media Houses Amid Political Dispute, Operations Disrupted

Bratislava, June 13—Production and distribution across Slovakia’s Media & Publishing sector have been disrupted for a second day after hundreds of protesters blockaded the headquarters and regional offices of several major news organizations, industry representatives said Thursday.

Demonstrators, who identify as supporters of the “Truth for Slovakia” movement, began staging coordinated blockades outside the main editorial offices of leading publishers in Bratislava, Košice, and Žilina early Wednesday morning. Protesters cite grievances over alleged political bias and coverage of recent government reforms, demanding editorial changes and resignations of senior editors.

Media outlets affected include national dailies Nova Pravda, Denný Spravodajca, and the major publishing house Východ Press, according to the Slovak Association of Publishers. “We are witnessing an unprecedented occupation of our sites. Editorial and printing staff are unable to enter their workplaces, halting production of today’s print editions,” said Martin Horváth, spokesperson for the association.

Journalists and press operators reported being prevented from accessing buildings, with some attempting to work remotely to maintain limited online updates. “We are doing our best to cover events in real time, but our newsrooms are offline and our print facilities are shut down,” said Lucia Kováčová, editor at Nova Pravda.

According to the Slovak Union of Media Workers, more than 1,200 employees across the industry have been unable to perform their regular duties. “Many workers have been stranded outside their offices since yesterday. The situation is tense, and some staff feel intimidated by the presence of large crowds,” said union chair Peter Varga.

Police have urged calm but have not moved to disperse the protesters as negotiations continue between movement leaders, publishers, and government mediators.

The Slovak Association of Publishers warned that if the blockade continues, the sector faces “severe operational and financial consequences,” with more print runs at risk and diminishing access to vital news coverage. No timeline has been given for a resolution, and the blockade remains in place at all major affected sites.
